correctness.rationale: For all m,n>=3 and all positive radii, the exact mixed-area cross coefficient follows from polygon support sums. Coprime arithmetic residues yield g copies of a consecutive M-term angular grid, whose Dirichlet cosine sum is B cos d. This proves the parity phase for all real angles including support ties. Normal-angle intersection uses the same congruence and contains exactly gcd(m,n) normals at area minima, so side counts and cusp are exact. Angular distribution and lcm asymptotic follow by integration and standard Taylor expansions. A separate convex-hull/shoelace program passed 3696 finite regressions with worst discrepancy below 2.14e-14; that is supporting regression, not an infinite proof.

evidence: Geigenfeind and de las Heras (2019) calculate identical regular polygons at angles, show explicit equilateral-triangle and square curves and plots for three through six sides; they are equivalent only to restricted equal-order instances.
Rotation profiles of excluded areas are Minkowski sums with an extra reversal of the second polygon. The present mixed-order formula can be converted to that convention by shifting the angle by pi.

originality.rationale: The read primary sources address equal-order angle responses, fixed relative angles for unlike polygons, general polygon normal-fan structure, or mixed-volume inequalities. Those statements do not contain or imply without an additional nontrivial arithmetic computation the complete two-order cos-distance law, gcd/lcm phase, exact coincidence of cusp minima with m+n-g facets and full area distribution. Known triangle/square, equal-order extrema, and fixed-orientation table values are explicitly credited and not counted as novel. Scholarly priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Absolute literature priority cannot be established by finite searches; a previously published arbitrary-pair angle formula could preempt the explicit theorem.
The 2014 identical-body minimization literature was checked via abstract only; it is acknowledged as covering the equal-order minimum statement, not ruled out by a full-text negative assessment.
A freely accessible regular-polytiles PDF was inspected in extracted text but not page images (page screenshot request returned HTTP 406).
The known 2019 regular polygon angle curves and 2026 fixed-orientation table values contain genuine special cases, which are excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: A single exact law explains all angular mixed areas of two regular polygons of unequal or equal side counts, including an arithmetic resonance leading to O(lcm(m,n)^-2) rather than a sidewise degree scaling, all extrema, nonsmooth side-count transition, and exact random-orientation law. The exact excluded-area profile is naturally motivated by orientation effects in hard-polygon mixtures and replaces brute edge-merging at every rotation; this is structural characterization rather than a trivial small-number recomputation.
